# A canvas draws what a program computes: shapes from a loop, shapes behind a
# condition, and shapes a program declared for itself.
#
# Four separate ways this produced a canvas with nothing in it. The shape
# lookup matched the spelling at the call site, so an aliased import of
# sngl:ui/draw drew a save and a restore with nothing between them. The walk
# looking for a canvas stopped at NodeInsts, so one inside an `if` was never
# lowered. The emitter read only NodeInst children, so a `for` and everything
# in it was dropped. And a shape composed of other shapes -- which is exempt
# from inlining, being rendered rather than composed away -- was emitted as a
# save/restore pair with its body left behind.

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out app.sngl

# The backing rect, then the loop: `for c = columns()` unrolls to two cells,
# and each expands to the three bars its body declares. The second cell's third
# bar sits at 30 + 16, which exists only if all of that happened.
grep 'ctx.fillRect\(0, 0, 60, 10\)' out/index.html
grep 'ctx.fillRect\(16, 0, 6, 6\)' out/index.html
grep 'ctx.fillRect\(46, 0, 6, 6\)' out/index.html

# And it redraws when the state it draws from changes. The dependency scan read
# only the draw function's top-level statements, so a canvas drawn from a loop
# looked like it depended on nothing and was painted once, at startup — and the
# handler's own write goes through an action it calls, which the scan did not
# follow either.
sngl dump --stage lowered --lang none --platform html app.sngl
stdout '__canvasRedraw'

# The TUI arm folds away, canvas and all.
sngl generate --platform bubbletea --lang go -o tui app.sngl
grep 'no pixels here' tui/model.go
! grep 'fillRect' tui/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "./gfx"
import "sngl:platform/bubbletea"

component main {
    var lit = true
    gfx.Panel(lit=lit)
    button(text="t", @click { lit!! })
}
-- gfx/gfx.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"
import "sngl:platform/bubbletea"

// An aliased import: the shapes are named draw.rect, not rect.
#[draw.shape]
component Bar(on = false, x = 0.0) {
    draw.rect(x=x, y=0.0, w=6.0, h=6.0, style=draw.CanvasStyle{fill=on ? #ff0000 : #003300})
}

// A shape made of shapes. It is not inlined away, so the canvas emitter has to
// expand it where it stands.
#[draw.shape]
component Cell(on = false, x = 0.0) {
    Bar(on=on, x=x)
    Bar(on=on, x=x + 8.0)
    Bar(on=on, x=x + 16.0)
}

func columns() => [0.0, 30.0]

// The canvas is one arm of a target test, and its shapes come from a loop.
component Panel(lit = false) {
    vbox {
        if PLATFORM == bubbletea.platform {
            text(value="no pixels here")
        } else {
            draw.canvas(width=60px, height=10px) {
                draw.rect(x=0.0, y=0.0, w=60.0, h=10.0, style=draw.CanvasStyle{fill=#000000})
                for c = columns() {
                    Cell(on=lit, x=c)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
